Both patches share a significant contract violation: Upload duplicates Add instead of routing through it, and neither tests source-reader failures.","reasons":["B’s retry test enables RetryAllMethods, matching the reported POST-upload scenario.","B verifies multipart content on both the initial request and retry, so an empty or truncated replay would be caught; A only counts requests.","B explicitly tests empty-filename and nil-content validation and confirms no request is made.","B’s multipart test separately checks media type, field name, filename, and bytes, giving clearer contract coverage than A’s ParseMultipartForm-based test."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add’s option handling, request execution, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of calling Add as required.","No tests cover validation or source-reader errors.","The retry test omits RetryAllMethods and does not inspect either request body, weakening coverage of the reported failure and replay correctness run on retries enabled for relevant method defaults/settings outside what the test demonstrates explicitly in the diff. As written, it does not faithfully reproduce the user’s configuration explicitly shown in the task prompt. It also omits confirming multipart body integrity on the retried call. A’s changelog adds detailed transport implementation claims that may become stale and are unnecessary for this focused change."],"risks_b":["Upload duplicates Add’s machinery instead of routing the encoded body through Add, violating the frozen contract and creating maintenance drift.","No test uses a failing source reader, so error propagation is unverified.","The retry input is already a bytes.Reader rather than a wrapped/non-seekable streamed reader, although the test does verify the helper-produced request body is fully replayed."]}
